answer: Throttle the inlet. Cap new keys at 200 per epoch network-wide, admitted by lottery seeded from a public randomness beacon, so nobody can buy the front of the line. Each admitted key must then build an unbroken thread of 5 passing answers in 5 consecutive epochs before any reward unlocks, and one miss resets the count. A farm wanting 1,000 keys waits through several lotteries, then must keep every key writing distinct passing answers for 5 more epochs, so its cost scales with time and labor, not key count.
